thumbnail_prompt: ONE image, both arms. The VIEWER, not a performer — measured 6.11% CTR for a person waking vs 3.03% for a musician playing. Dawn light across a doorway, a person standing barefoot with a cup, unhurried, looking out. Pichwai/Kangra miniature, aged parchment ground, ornate border. A bansuri may rest at the frame edge; it must NOT be the subject, and must not be held or played. Text in its own banner panel at ~35% of frame, second tier 'Bansuri · Raga Bhairav'. Legible at 120px.
suno_prompt: Instrumental only, no vocals, no humming — gentle Indian classical bansuri in Raga Bhairav, breath-driven bamboo flute with long sustained notes and natural breath pauses, flat 2nd and flat 6th for a grounding morning quality, no percussion, steady tanpura drone, 70 BPM, seamless loop.
suno_prompt_note: Built to data/suno_prompt_patterns.md. Short one-liner (283 chars, band is 180-300). NO 'slow' — banked: that word makes Suno drag, and it is reserved for sleep/deep-rest only; morning uses 'gentle' and sets tempo with the NUMBER. 70 BPM = top of the morning-breathwork band (60-70), per the 'BPM at the top of the band for morning' rule. NO TABLA — Bansuri rule, stated as 'no percussion'. Physical descriptor is the banked one for bansuri. Raga Bhairav named with its one defining characteristic; unused on this channel. ⚠ RUN tools/claim_check.py ON THE CLIP BEFORE RENDERING.

runtime_note: 1 HOUR, not 1.5. Two reasons. (1) CLONE: Bansuri x morning x 1.5hr last ran 2026-08-31 ('Calm Morning Music | Relaxing Flute'), 19 days out and inside the 21-day window — and that ship took 1,300 engaged, the best of its fortnight, so a near-identical package would compete with something that is working. At 1hr the last comparable ship is 2026-05-05, 137 days clear. (2) It is the format that WON this cell: 'Productive Day Music | Positive Morning Vibes | 1 Hour Bansuri Session' is the cell's best at 4,203 engaged, and it holds 29.3 min AVD on a 60-min runtime (49%) against ~23% for the channel's 1.5hr ships. Shorter runtime, better proportional retention.
